title: Farza on rejoining Y Combinator at 30: building again with hard-won experience
summary: A personal essay where Farza explains why he is joining YC a second time at 30 without a fixed idea. He contrasts the naivety of founding at 23 with the clarity of 30, and why he chooses to build over taking a safer job or VC path. Mindset-focused, with little tactical growth content.

principles.text: You will never feel fully ready to start a company, so go for it anyway.
principles.quote: I feel like I'll never be “ready” so just gotta go for it. Yolo baby.

principles.text: Pair beginner's naivety with the hard-won experience of having built before.
principles.quote: Still, I feel like I have the naivety of a 19 year-old, but, with the mental of a guy who’s been through a lot and learned a lot.

principles.text: You don't need a specific idea to start; act on the pull to explore your ideas to avoid regret.
principles.quote: it’s more a feeling of “I should explore my ideas...I would regret it if I didn’t”.

principles.text: Choose the riskier path of building when your vision keeps nagging you, even if safer jobs are on offer.
principles.quote: every time I think about getting a job (of which I’ve been offered many great ones) that voice in my head comes back and says to give my visions a shot.

principles.text: Timing matters: major technology shifts are the best moment to work on your ideas.
principles.quote: There’s never been a better time to work on the ideas in my head.

principles.text: Spend time building rather than documenting; keep updates lightweight.
principles.quote: I’m not going to spend a lot of time documenting. Will mostly be focused on building.
